5 Free Computer Science Schools in Germany for International Students Skip to content 5 Free Computer Science Schools in Germany for International Students Hyun Lee | April 3rd, 2026 | 0 comments on 5 Free Computer Science Schools in Germany for International Students | Search Courses: Any Degree Undergraduate Masters MBA Any Subject Business Computer Science Data Science Design Finance Marketing Any Country Europe Germany France Spain Search Germany is one of the most attractive destinations for international students who want to study computer science without paying high tuition fees. Many public universities in Germany charge no tuition for most bachelor’s and master’s programs, making it possible to earn a respected degree while keeping costs low. For students interested in fields such as artificial intelligence, software development, data science, and cybersecurity, Germany offers strong academic programs, modern research facilities, and excellent career opportunities in one of Europe’s leading technology and innovation hubs. Although students usually still pay a semester contribution, the overall cost is far lower than in many other countries, which is why free universities in Germany for computer science continue to attract students from around the world. If you are interested, check out these open computer science courses in Germany can also compare programs by degree level, subject area, and tuition fee more easily. Find Open Courses in Germany University Current Semester Fee Saarland University €394.30 per semester University of Potsdam €354.80 per semester FH Aachen €366.60 per semester RPTU University Kaiserslautern-Landau €348.80 per semester University of Duisburg-Essen €349.80 per semester Free Computer Science Schools in Germany 1. Saarland University Computer Science Programs | Free Tuition | Admissions | Scholarships Free to: Bachelor’s, Master’s Saarland University is one of the strongest free universities in Germany for students interested in computer science. Its computer science ecosystem is closely tied to the Saarland Informatics Campus, which brings together the university’s department with major research institutes and creates a highly research-focused study environment. This makes the university especially attractive for students who want a serious academic setting in areas like artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, software systems, and theoretical computer science. For students searching for free universities in Germany for computer science, Saarland University stands out because standard first-degree and consecutive Master’s programmes do not charge tuition fees, even though a semester fee still applies. The university also offers strong English-accessible options in computer science, including an English-taught bachelor’s programme and a research-driven master’s pathway, making it a practical choice for international students who want a low-cost education with excellent academic depth. 2. University of Potsdam Computer Science Programs | Free Tuition | Admissions | Scholarships Free to: Bachelor’s, Master’s Computer Science offerings at the University of Potsdam are presented as part of a broad and interdisciplinary academic environment, with connections to engineering, natural sciences, cognitive sciences, economics, biology, and earth science. This makes it especially attractive for students who want a Computer Science education that goes beyond a narrow technical track. Apply for 2026 Intake! Applications for 2026 Intake are open. Search degrees around the world! Apply now For affordability, the university stands out because it does not charge tuition for undergraduate programs and consecutive master’s programs, which is a major advantage for Computer Science students seeking low-cost study options in Germany. While students still need to cover semester fees and living expenses, the combination of public-university pricing, research links in the Potsdam-Berlin area, and a well-developed Computer Science ecosystem gives the University of Potsdam excellent value. 3. FH Aachen Computer Science Programs | Free Tuition | Admissions | Scholarships Free to: Bachelor’s, Master’s FH Aachen is a public university of applied sciences with a practice-focused Computer Science B.Sc and M.Sc. The program is designed to combine core computing foundations with hands-on learning, and students can build depth through areas such as software engineering, IT security, IT management, media informatics, computer engineering, and autonomous systems/visual computing. For affordability, FH Aachen does not charge regular tuition, although students do pay a semester contribution for student services and transport-related benefits. This makes it especially attractive for both domestic and international students who want a career-oriented computer science education in Germany without standard tuition fees, while still having access to admissions guidance and scholarship information. “The ‘free tuition’ fee attracts me… it gives me more freedom in exploring what I am interested in.” Shafiq , Bachelor’s in Computer Science at FH Aachen University of Applied Sciences 4. RPTU University Kaiserslautern-Landau Computer Science Programs | Free Tuition | Admissions | Scholarships Free to: Bachelor’s, Master’s The Department of Computer Science at RPTU University Kaiserslautern-Landau offers Computer Science at both the bachelor’s and master’s levels, making it suitable for students who want a full academic pathway at a public German university. This makes RPTU especially appealing for students seeking a recognized computer science school without the high tuition costs found in many other countries. Check Currently Open Courses! Check these courses that are currently open for international students! Apply now For affordability, RPTU stands out because the university states that bachelor’s degrees and consecutive master’s degrees remain free of charge, although students should still expect semester-based administrative contributions and possible assessment or application-related fees depending on their case. 5. University of Duisburg-Essen Computer Science Programs | Free Tuition | Admissions | Scholarships Free to: Bachelor’s, Master’s The computer science offerings at the University of Duisburg-Essen are broad and practical, with degree paths connected to core informatics as well as related areas such as software engineering, business informatics, computer engineering, cyber-physical systems, and human-centered computing. This makes it a good fit for students who want a tuition-free university with multiple computing directions under one institution. The university stands out because it does not charge tuition fees, which is one of the biggest advantages of studying computer science at a public university in Germany. Students should still expect a semester contribution for student services and transport, and many programs are primarily taught in German, so language preparation can be important depending on the degree. Overall, the University of Duisburg-Essen is a practical and affordable choice for students seeking computer science education in Germany with access to a large academic environment and several specialized study options. “I believe that computer engineering is one of the most important and future-oriented professions.” Ayse Yaren Bato , Deutschlandstipendium scholar at University of Duisburg-Essen FAQs: Free Computer Science Schools in Germany Which tuition-free German university is best for research-focused computer science? Saarland University is one of the strongest choices for students who want a serious research-focused computer science environment. Its ties to the Saarland Informatics Campus make it especially attractive for areas such as artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, software systems, and theoretical computer science. Do I need German to study computer science in Germany? It depends on the university and the specific program. Some computer science options are more English-accessible, while others are primarily taught in German. Students should always check the language of instruction before applying, especially at universities where many programs are still mainly German-taught. Are scholarships still useful if computer science tuition is already free in Germany? Yes. Even when tuition is waived, scholarships can still help cover living expenses, semester contributions, transport, application costs, and other study-related expenses. That is why scholarship such as DAAD Scholarships and Deutschlandstipendium remains useful for international students planning to study computer science in Germany. I hope that this article on free computer science schools in Germany was helpful! If you are interested, check out the Germany Study Guide and Open Courses in Germany for International Students !
